possible_causes: Pump operating away from the intended operating point
Air or gas entering the suction line
troubleshooting: Compare the current operating point with the pump's intended operating range
Inspect the suction line and strainer for restriction or blockage
Check for air ingress at suction fittings and seals
Verify valve positions on suction and discharge lines
solutions: Repair air leaks at suction fittings
Adjust operating point closer to design conditions

possible_causes: Pump operating away from the intended operating point
Air or gas entering the suction flow
Wear ring or internal clearance wear
troubleshooting: Check suction conditions and strainer
Check for air entering the suction flow
Inspect for restrictions in suction and discharge lines
Compare pressure gauge readings with rated performance
solutions: Repair leaks introducing air into the flow
Replace worn internal clearances if wear is confirmed

possible_causes: Operation at low-flow or off-design conditions
troubleshooting: Measure vibration levels where monitoring equipment is available
Check for cavitation symptoms (noise, pressure fluctuation)
Inspect inlet piping for turbulence-causing fittings
Check coupling and shaft alignment
solutions: Avoid sustained operation far from the intended operating range
Correct alignment between pump and driver

possible_causes: High losses in the suction system
troubleshooting: Evaluate NPSH available versus NPSH required
Inspect suction piping for excessive losses
Check suction lift and fluid temperature
Listen for characteristic crackling/gravel-like noise
solutions: Use appropriately sized suction piping and low-loss fittings
Reduce suction lift or improve suction conditions
Consider a bypass or control method to avoid damaging low-flow operation

troubleshooting: Check how long the pump has run at low or no flow
Check bearing condition and lubrication
Check for cavitation symptoms
Monitor casing and bearing temperature
solutions: Avoid prolonged low-flow or shut-off operation
Address the root cause of cavitation if present

troubleshooting: Identify whether the noise is hydraulic (cavitation-like) or mechanical (grinding/knocking)
Check bearing condition
Inspect inlet piping configuration
Check for unbalance
solutions: Address cavitation causes if hydraulic noise is confirmed

safety_precautions: Shut down the pump before maintenance
Isolate the pump from its energy source and follow approved Lockout/Tagout procedures
Depressurize the system before opening it
Safely handle hazardous or hot liquid
Wear appropriate PPE
Do not inspect rotating components while exposed and operating
Follow the manufacturer's specific maintenance instructions

troubleshooting: Measure vibration where monitoring equipment is available
Check alignment of the shaft and associated components
Inspect mounting for looseness or incorrect fit
Inspect for contamination
solutions: Rebalance the machine if load imbalance is identified
Clean contamination and replace affected lubricant

troubleshooting: Check operating temperature against normal conditions
Inspect lubrication condition and check for leakage
Check alignment
Inspect for excessive load conditions
solutions: Apply the correct lubricant type and quantity

troubleshooting: Listen for abnormal noise and characterize it (grinding, squeaking, irregular)
Inspect lubrication condition
During shutdown, inspect bearing condition for marks, scratches, or discoloration
Check alignment
solutions: Align the shaft and associated components

troubleshooting: Inspect the bearing surface for marks, scratches, discoloration, or wear during shutdown
Check lubrication history
Check alignment and mounting
solutions: Replace a worn or damaged bearing

troubleshooting: Inspect lubrication condition and quantity
Check for leakage past seals
Verify lubricant type against manufacturer recommendation
solutions: Apply the correct lubricant type and quantity

troubleshooting: Observe unusual shaft movement or looseness
Check bearing clearance against specification
Inspect mounting and shaft fit
solutions: Correct excessive looseness or incorrect fit
Replace the bearing if wear has caused excessive clearance

safety_precautions: Shut down the machine before detailed inspection
Follow the facility's approved isolation procedure
Prevent accidental machine startup
Use appropriate PPE
Use correct bearing mounting and dismounting tools
Follow lubricant and chemical safety requirements
Do not touch rotating components during operation

possible_causes: Air demand exceeds compressor delivery capacity
troubleshooting: Check pressure settings against the compressor's instruction manual
Check the air filter for blockage
Inspect valves, hoses, and connections for leakage
Compare air demand with compressor delivery capacity
solutions: Ensure compressor capacity matches system demand

troubleshooting: Check cooling airflow and ventilation around the compressor
Check oil level
Inspect the cooler for dirt or blockage
Check cooling-water flow and temperature where applicable
solutions: Remove cooling-air restrictions and improve room ventilation
Have severely clogged cooling components serviced

troubleshooting: Check the power supply and protection devices
Check for a tripped overload or circuit breaker
Check phase sequence and wiring continuity
solutions: Reset an overload once, only where permitted by the manufacturer's procedure
Check electrical connections and phase sequence
If the fault persists, obtain qualified technical service

troubleshooting: Check control components such as the solenoid and inlet valve
Inspect control-air tubing for leaks
solutions: Inspect and free the inlet valve
Repair or replace leaking control-air tubing

safety_precautions: Isolate the compressor from the power supply before inspection or maintenance
Release all system pressure before opening panels
Follow the machine's specified isolation procedure
Do not open panels or inspect internal components until safely isolated
Follow the manufacturer's model-specific safety instructions
Use appropriate PPE
Have complex repairs performed by qualified personnel
